body.p: The AI Positron add-on installed in can function as a local MCP (Model Context Protocol) HTTP server. This allows third-party AI assistants installed on your own computer such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Open Code, or Cursor to connect and use all tools defined and contributed by AI Positron. These include tools for validating XML, refactoring, running XPath, finding in files, reading and editing content, and accessing the current editor context (the opened project, files, currently edited files, and the current selection).

Configure and start the server in the
Preferences Plugins / Oxygen AI Positron / Oxygen MCP Server page.

dd.p: The port number on which the local MCP HTTP server listens for incoming connections. The default port is 8757. Change this value if the default port is already in use by another application. The port can be changed only while the server is stopped.

A button that starts or stops the local MCP HTTP server. The first time you click Start, you must accept an End User License Agreement (EULA) before the server can run. After the initial acceptance, the EULA is not displayed again for subsequent starts and stops.

When the server is running, third-party AI assistants can discover and call the tools provided by AI Positron.The server must be started manually each time you restart the application, unless the Remember the server state (running or stopped) and restore it at application start option is selected.The MCP HTTP server can be started only if you are using Enterprise version or the AI Positron Enterprise license.
This feature gives the ability to an LLM used by a third party AI Assistant to read, modify, and delete your local files using AI Positron provided tools.
By enabling the MCP Feature, you agree to the following:
You are solely responsible for the configuration, security, and all consequences of any automated use of the editor application via the MCP Feature.
You knowingly and expressly assume all risks associated with this automated use. These risks include, but are not limited to modification, corruption, or deletion of your local files and data or disclosure or exfiltration of your data to third-party services.

dlentry.dt: Remember the server state (running or stopped) and restore it at application start

dd.p: If selected, remembers whether you last left the server running or stopped, and restores that state the next time it starts. The server does not run while the application is closed. If you left the server running in the previous session, it starts again automatically after the application's main window is displayed. If you had stopped it, it remains stopped. The server starts with the same port and authentication token, so AI assistants that you have already connected do not require a new configuration. This option is not selected by default.

The server starts automatically only after you accept the EULA by clicking Start once. If the server cannot start (for example, because another application is already using its port), the page shows the server as stopped. The application attempts to start it again the next time starts.

Displayed while the server is running. The server accepts connections only from the local computer, at http://127.0.0.1:port/mcp (for example, http://127.0.0.1:8757/mcp for the default port). It uses the MCP Streamable HTTP transport only; the older HTTP with SSE transport is not supported, so configure the AI assistant to connect using Streamable HTTP.

Copies the MCP configuration JSON to the clipboard. Paste this configuration into your AI assistant's MCP settings to establish the connection. The copied configuration includes the port and a unique authentication token. Once added, the AI assistant will be able to discover and call the XML tools available in the AI Positron add-on.
The authentication token is kept when you stop and start the server, change the port, or restart . After changing the port, copy the configuration again, since the server URL changes.

Stops the server if it is running, resets the port to its default value, deselects the Remember the server state (running or stopped) and restore it at application start option, and generates a new authentication token. AI assistants that were configured with the previous token are rejected (with an HTTP 401 Unauthorized error) until you click Copy MCP Configuration and paste the new configuration into each of them. Use this button to revoke the access of all the AI assistants that you previously connected.

section.title: Tools
section.p:
All AI tools that are part of the AI Positron add-on are available through the use of the HTTP MCP server to the third-party AI Assistant, with the exception of the following tools, which have no use or no safe use for an AI assistant connected through the HTTP MCP server:
run_command_line - The AI assistant runs commands through its own tools, with its own restrictions.
search_chat_history - Past AI Positron conversations can contain content that you did not intend to share again. AI Positron asks for your approval before this tool runs in its chat, but there is no such approval process for a call made through the HTTP MCP server.
ask_user - The tool asks its questions in the AI Positron chat. The AI assistant asks you through its own interface instead.
store_to_memory and update_memory - The tools manage the memory of the AI Positron chat. The AI assistant has a memory of its own.
section.note: The approval prompt that AI Positron displays before running an unsafe tool applies only to its own chat. Tools called by a third-party AI assistant through the HTTP MCP server run without any prompt from AI Positron, including tools that modify files, such as edit_document. Approving tool calls is the responsibility of the third-party AI assistant, so configure its own tool permission settings accordingly.
section.p: AI Tools contributed by the main application and other installed plugins which are loaded by the AI Positron add-on also become available through the started HTTP MCP server.

In addition the following specific tools are available through the HTTP MCP server:
get_oxygen_xml_application_context Retrieves context information obtained from the open application, including the project context prompt configured by the user, information about the documents open in the editor and DITA Maps Manager, information about the currently selected document (including the content selected inside it), and the list of skills available to be loaded.
open_document_in_oxygen_xml_application Instructs to open a document and make it the currently edited document. If the document is already open, it is selected as the currently edited document.

section.title: Changes Made to the Same Document at the Same Time
section.p: Several AI assistants connected through the HTTP MCP server, or an AI assistant and the AI Positron chat, can modify files at the same time. Changes to different documents are made in parallel. Changes to the same document are made one at a time: each tool call reads the document only after the previous change was saved, so no change is lost. This applies to the tools that modify a document: edit_document, save_document, refactor_xml, refactor_xml_with_xslt, and add_dita_reference_to_ditamap.

ul.li: If another change already modified the text that an edit replaces, the edit fails with an error saying that the text could not be located. The AI assistant is expected to read the document again and retry the edit.

If a change waits for more than 30 seconds for another change of the same document to end, it fails with an error telling the AI assistant to retry. This can happen, for example, while another change of that document is waiting for you to confirm it.

section.note: A tool call that writes the entire content of a document replaces whatever the document contains at that moment. If the AI assistant read the content before another change was made, that change is overwritten. Edits that replace specific text, the usual way of editing with edit_document, are not affected.

section.title: Server Status and Changed Files
section.p: The Oxygen MCP Server button in the AI Positron view toolbar shows the HTTP MCP server status and the documents that external AI assistants have changed through the server. If you have the Enterprise license required to start the server, the button is always displayed, even when the server is stopped. Otherwise, it is displayed only when the server is running or when changed documents are waiting for review.

A badge in the lower-right corner of the button icon indicates the server status:
A green dot - The server is running, and no documents are waiting for review.
A number in a green bubble - The server is running, and the number indicates how many changed documents are waiting for review. If more than nine documents are waiting, the bubble displays a star.
A number in a grey bubble - The server is stopped, but documents changed while it was running are still waiting for review.
No badge - The server is not running, and no documents are waiting for review.
Hover over the button to view the same information in its tooltip, including the exact number of documents waiting for review.

Click the button to open the Oxygen MCP Server dialog box. The dialog box shows the Server status, the server URL when the server is running, and a Server preferences link that opens this preferences page, where you can start or stop the server. When the server is stopped, the dialog box also explains the server's purpose. Below this information, it lists the documents that external AI assistants changed through the edit tool provided by AI Positron. You can review the changes and accept, modify, or reject them. The server status and document list are updated while the dialog box is open.
